cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Hi Alex. It’s Martha Clines here. James White gave me your number. I hope you don’t mind me calling you.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Of course not. How are you, Martha?

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Good thanks. I’m ringing because I need a bit of advice.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Oh yeah. What about?

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: The training you did at JPNW a few years ago. I’m applying for the same thing.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Oh right. Yes, I did mine in 2014 (Example). Best thing I ever did. I’m still working there.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Really? What are you doing?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Well, now I work in the customer services department but I did my initial training in Finance (Q1). I stayed there for the first two years and then moved to where I am now.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: That’s the same department I’m applying for. Did you enjoy it?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: I was pretty nervous to begin with. I didn’t do well in my exams at school and I was really worried because I failed Maths (Q2). But it didn’t actually matter because I did lots of courses on the job.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Did you get a diploma at the end of your trainee period? I’m hoping to do the one in business skills.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Yes. That sounds good. I took the one on IT skills but I wish I’d done that one instead. (Q3)

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: OK, that’s good to know. What about the other trainees? How did you get on with them?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: There were about 20 of us who started at the same time and we were all around the same age - I was 18 and there was only one person younger than me, how was 17 (Q4). The rest were between 18 and 20. I made some good friends.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: I’ve heard lots of good things about the training at JPNW. It seems like there are a lot of opportunities there.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Yeah, definitely. Because of its size you can work in loads of different areas within the organisation.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: What about pay? I know you get a lower minimum wage than regular employees.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: That’s right - which isn’t great. Buy you get the same number of days’ holiday as everyone else (Q5). And the pay goes up massively if they offer you a job at the end of the training period.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Yeah, but I’m not doing it for the money - it’s the experience I think will be really useful. Everyone says by the end of the year you gain so much confidence.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: You’re right. That’s the most useful part about it. There’s a lot of variety too. You’re given lots of different things to do. I enjoyed it all - I didn’t even mind the studying.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Do you have to spend any time in college?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Yes, one day each month (Q6). So you get lots of support from both your tutor and your manager.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: That’s good. And the company is easy to get to, isn’t it?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Yes, it’s very close to the train station so the location’s a real advantage. (Q7)

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Have you got a date for your interview yet?

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Yes, it’s on the 23rd of this month.

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: So long as you’re well prepared there’s nothing to worry about. Everyone’s very friendly.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: I am not sure what I should wear. What do you think?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Nothing too casual - like jeans (Q8), for example. If you’ve got a nice jacket, wear that with a skirt or trousers.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: OK. Thanks. Any other tips?

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Erm, well I know it’s really obvious but arrive in plenty of time (Q9). They hate people who are late. So make sure you know exactly where you have to get to. And one other useful piece of advice my manager told me before I had the interview for this job - is to smile (Q10). Even if you feel terrified. It makes people respond better to you.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: I’ll have to practise doing that in the mirror!

cues.speaker: ALEX
cues.text: Yeah - well, good luck. Let me know if you need any more information.

cues.speaker: MARTHA
cues.text: Thanks very much.
